newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax says it is predator, not prey.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax says it is predator, not prey.

text.p: OfficeMax is predator, not prey, in terms of acquisitions, chairman and chief executive officer Michael Feuer said on Friday.

Asked to comment on a November 25 Business Week magazine story that said the 530-store office supply retailer might be either an acquisition target or an acquirer in continuing industry consolidation, Feuer said in a telephone interview, "I've said publicly... we are the predator, not the prey."
Feuer, who is also a founder of the company, said, "Any acquisition would have to be accretive to earnings and (provide) further enhancement of the OfficeMax name."
In September its top competitors, Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc, proposed a stock-swap merger.
Feuer also said that OfficeMax plans by year-end to announce a joint venture with "a premier company in Japan."
On Friday afternoon, OfficeMax stock was up 3/8 to 14-3/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Feuer said the company has accelerated its new store plans, expanded new venues such as its in-store copy centers and furniture centers and expanded internationally.
A joint venture store opened recently in Mexico is "far exceeding expectations," he said.
"OfficeMax thinks outside the box. We will look at anything where we can leverage our assets and capabilities, enhance shareholder value ... and further enhance the OfficeMax name," Feuer said.
That could mean acquisitions or other expansion of its various concepts, including its DirectMax business-to-business operations, which now consist of catalog sales, he said.
In addition, he said it could look to related services such as temporary office help, although he said that is not currently in the plan.
